narrative.goal: Research and redesign the web glass-refraction effect toward a remarkably simple, cross-browser, cross-platform, performant API for native-like glass (broader than tw-glass / Tailwind).
narrative.next: Go deep on the current refraction implementation (packages/tw-glass/scripts/filter-builder.mjs displacement map + feDisplacementMap, generate.mjs), then survey and empirically prototype alternative techniques (inline SVG filters, layered masks, WebGL/WebGPU or canvas shader overlays, CSS Houdini Paint API, native Liquid Glass parallels), comparing fidelity, cross-browser support, performance, and API simplicity in the browser harness (Chromium + real Safari).
narrative.state_markdown:
- Worktree .claude/worktrees/tw-glass-updates on branch tw-glass-updates (off origin/main 4dfc5da01). Two commits this session, NOT pushed: c8d04d084 feat(tw-glass) glass-frosted + backdrop hardening; 96dd3d274 refactor(docs) demo consolidation + a11y/perf.
- Current refraction tech: an SVG displacement-map (data URI) referenced from backdrop-filter via url(). GLASS_BACKDROP_FILTER = var(--tw-glass-filter) + frost; GLASS_FROST_FILTER is frost-only (blur/brightness/saturate). Generated by packages/tw-glass/scripts/{filter-builder.mjs,generate.mjs} into src/index.css.
- CRITICAL empirical browser findings (verified in REAL Safari + Chromium this session): refraction renders ONLY in Chromium. Safari applies NO SVG filter reference in backdrop-filter, neither a data URI nor an inline url(#id) fragment; it supports only primitive functions (blur, brightness, saturate). Firefox likewise does not apply SVG filter refs in backdrop-filter.
- Because the displacement url() is composed into a SINGLE backdrop-filter value, Safari/Firefox drop the ENTIRE property (no blur fallback). Two-declaration fallback fails (Safari treats the url value as valid and overrides the plain one). No @supports query distinguishes parses-vs-renders. A layered ::before cannot reproduce the single-line displace-then-blur: blur-on-box muddies refraction (worse as blur rises); displace-on-box + blur-on-::before loses blur in Chromium and is starved in Safari.
- Shipped this session: glass-frosted (cross-browser frosted base, no refraction) as the universal alternative; glass stays the Chromium refraction. README reframed to pick-one-base; browser-support docs corrected.
- Perf snapshot: stress page renders ~136 backdrop-filter layers; idle ~120fps drops to ~56fps under heavy scroll with ~14 percent of frames over 32ms; content-visibility auto gave no measurable benefit on a full sweep. Hero mousemove lighting gated on prefers-reduced-motion + IntersectionObserver.
- Tooling ready: agent-browser drives Chromium via CDP; real Safari driven via osascript (set URL of front document) plus screencapture region (-R x,y,w,h); standalone test pages generated from the package filter-builder (see /tmp/gen-glass-test*.mjs and /tmp/gen-frosted-test.mjs). Dev server: BUILD packages first (pnpm exec turbo build filtered to ./packages) or runtime imports like assistant-cloud fail module-not-found; then pnpm --filter @assistant-ui/docs exec next dev -p 3005 (port 3000 taken by another project). All routes incl / verified 200.
narrative.debt_markdown:
- North star is API SIMPLICITY: current tw-glass surface (many glass-* classes that silently override each other and behave differently per browser) was flagged as poor DX; the redesign must avoid that.
- Hard constraint: pure-CSS backdrop-filter SVG displacement is Chromium-only. To hit cross-browser AND cross-platform, next session should seriously evaluate non-backdrop-filter rendering (WebGL/WebGPU, canvas, Houdini Paint API, or a JS-assisted approach), accepting that may mean relaxing the no-JS / Tailwind-only constraint.
- Cross-platform likely includes React Native / native targets (monorepo has @assistant-ui/react-native) and Apple native Liquid Glass as a fidelity reference; scope what cross-platform means with the user early.
- Branch tw-glass-updates is generically named and unpushed; consider renaming before any PR. REVIEW.md, REVIEW-findings.json, and .circuit/ were intentionally left untracked (generated/tooling artifacts).
- Open: whether to add a live glass-frosted demo page to the docs (offered, not yet done).
